title: Stratum telemetry atelier: per-route & per-model performance glyphs
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Design a compact, scannable 'atelier' view for per-route and per-model telemetry that surfaces latency distributions, token quanta, throughput, and cost attribution via a set of reusable visual 'glyphs' and miniature charts. The goal is a single-pane summary for SREs and PMs with fast drill paths into full signal explorers.
background: Console analytics heatmaps and large canvas dashboards are effective for deep dives but are noisy for day-to-day ops. Teams asked for a lightweight, glanceable row for each route/model that conveys health, cost pressure, recent regressions, and the dominant token/latency patterns. We want to standardize a glyph system so product pages, rollout cards, and alerts speak the same visual language.
goals: Create a 1-row summary layout (glyph + microcharts) for model-route entries
Design a set of 6 reusable glyphs (latency seam, throughput bar, token quanta, error spike, cache hit, cost slice)
Define consistent chart specs for micro area/histogram/stacked bar visualizations suitable for 40–160px height
Prototype interactive drilldowns from glyphs to the model-route performance canvas and trace view
Validate readability at 1280x720 and in dense lists (10+ rows)
deliverables: Figma prototype: 'Stratum list' with 3 density modes (compact | standard | verbose)
Chart spec doc with recommended data shapes, aggregation windows, color tokens, and accessibility contrast targets
Design tokens for small-viewport sparkline and histogram variants
Interaction spec for hover, expand, and inline canary rollout overlays
Developer handoff with CSS grid snippets and SVG glyphs
chart_specs: Latency Seam (micro-area): 120x36 px; stacked percentile bands (p50/p90/p99); data points: per-10s aggregation; stroke: 1px; fill: gradient from #E9F5FF to transparent; hover shows percentile breakouts

Token Quanta Histogram: 140x44 px; 8 bins; logarithmic x-axis mapping for prompt+completion token counts; bar gap 2px; colors: low=#E6F8E6, mid=#FFF6E0, high=#FFEFE6; tooltip: sample count, median latency for that bin

Throughput Sparkbar: 100x16 px; minibars representing requests/sec per minute; baseline line for SLA throughput; color ramp from blue to purple for load intensity; keyboard focus exposes exact rps numbers
Cost Slice Mini-Donut: 40x40 px; shows percent of route cost relative to model group for last 24h; 3 segments: inference, cache, overhead; labeled for screen readers with aria-label summary
Cache-hit Gauge: semicircular arc 80x40 px; shows percent cache-hit; ticks at 25/50/75; color thresholds (green >=80, amber 50-79, red <50); animated delta when change >5% over hour
Error Spike Flag: single-pixel heatline overlay; binary state + count badge; displays latest 1m error rate and rolling alert boolean
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Ellis): prefer token histogram y-axis showing median latency, not raw count — helps prioritize high-cost bins
Eng (Priya Nair): request simplified data model: 1-minute buckets with precomputed percentiles to avoid client-side aggregation
SRE (Marco Alvarez): color thresholds for cache-hit gauge should be configurable per-customer SLA
Accessibility (Rina Patel): ensure donut and gauge have text fallbacks and 4.5:1 contrast for core states
decisions: Adopt 1-minute aggregation cadence for list glyphs to align with backend metrics retention
Ship three density modes; default is 'standard' with compact as opt-in for high-cardinality lists
Use precomputed p50/p90/p99 histograms from telemetry pipeline instead of client aggregation
Expose per-route color token overrides in Console theme settings (enterprise feature)
tradeoffs: Using 1-minute aggregation reduces noise but hides sub-minute spikes — mitigated by drilldowns to high-resolution microtraces
Glyph micro-charts prioritize scanability over full data fidelity; some numeric precision sacrificed to keep row height small
Adding configurable thresholds increases backend complexity for Dedicated/Private customers but improves SRE signal relevance
